Edit and run the cells below, in order. The first visit may take a minute to load.
Copy any code you want to keep before leaving or reloading the page.

The endpoints, parameters and response fields used here are described in the
[Proteins API reference](../docs/mgnify-proteins-api.md).
For exhaustive queries, combined filters and large sequence sets, use the
[programmatic access guide](../docs/mgnify-proteins-programmatic.md).

## Set up

Every example reuses this base address and helper.

```{pyodide}
import requests

API = "https://www.ebi.ac.uk/metagenomics/proteins/api/v1"

def get_json(path, **params):
    response = requests.get(f"{API}/{path}", params=params, timeout=30)
    response.raise_for_status()
    return response.json()

def search_proteins(*, limit=50, biome_id=None, biome_lineage=None, pfam_accession=None):
    filters = {
        key: value for key, value in {
            "biome_id": biome_id,
            "biome_lineage": biome_lineage,
            "pfam_accession": pfam_accession,
        }.items() if value is not None
    }
    if len(filters) != 1:
        raise ValueError("Provide exactly one biome or Pfam filter")
    if type(limit) is not int or not 1 <= limit <= 1000:
        raise ValueError("limit must be an integer from 1 to 1000")
    hits = get_json("protein/search", limit=limit, **filters)
    if len(hits) == limit:
        print(
            f"Search reached limit={limit}; results may be incomplete. "
            "Use release files for all matches. There is no next page."
        )
    return hits

print(API)
```

## Look up a protein

Fetch one cluster representative and read its sequence. Replace the accession to
look up a different protein.

```{pyodide}
protein = get_json("protein/MGYP000261684433")

print(protein["mgyp"])
print(f"{len(protein['sequence'])} aa")
print({True: "full-length", False: "fragment", None: "unknown"}[protein["full_length"]])
```

The same record written out as FASTA:

```{pyodide}
print(f">{protein['mgyp']}\n{protein['sequence']}")
```

## Find proteins carrying a Pfam domain

The search endpoint takes **exactly one** filter. Searching by Pfam accession
returns the matching cluster representatives:

```{pyodide}
hits = search_proteins(pfam_accession="PF00005", limit=5)

for hit in hits:
    print(hit["mgyp"])
```

Search results carry only `mgyp`, `full_length` and `cluster_size`. Fetching each
hit from the detail endpoint adds the sequence length and the domains it carries:

```{pyodide}
for hit in hits:
    protein = get_json(f"protein/{hit['mgyp']}")
    domains = ", ".join(p["accession"] for p in protein["pfam_annotations"])
    length = {True: "full-length", False: "fragment", None: "unknown"}[protein["full_length"]]
    print(f"{protein['mgyp']}\t{length}\t{len(protein['sequence'])} aa\t{domains}")
```

## Build a limited FASTA file for a biome

A common workflow: find the cluster representatives observed in a biome, then
retrieve each sequence. Searching by `biome_lineage` covers the biome **and all of
its sub-biomes**. Edit the lineage or the limit, then run the cell again to rebuild
the download.

This is a limited selection ordered by MGYP, not all sequences in the biome or a
random sample. Every run that reaches `LIMIT` prints a warning. `offset`, `page`
and `cursor` are ignored by the service; they cannot retrieve the rest of the
results.

```{pyodide}
#| define: [fasta_text, fasta_filename]
LINEAGE = "root:Engineered:Wastewater"
LIMIT = 10

hits = search_proteins(biome_lineage=LINEAGE, limit=LIMIT)

records = []
for hit in hits:
    protein = get_json(f"protein/{hit['mgyp']}")
    records.append(f">{protein['mgyp']}\n{protein['sequence']}")

fasta_text = "\n".join(records) + "\n"
fasta_filename = LINEAGE.replace(":", "-") + f"-limit-{LIMIT}.fasta"

print(f"Collected {len(records)} sequences")
print(fasta_text[:240] + "...")
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
fasta_text = ""
fasta_filename = ""

fasta_text && fasta_filename
  ? DOM.download(new Blob([fasta_text], {type: "text/plain;charset=utf-8"}), fasta_filename, "Download FASTA")
  : html`<p>Run the cell above to prepare the FASTA download.</p>`
```

::: {.callout-note}
`requests` encodes the query parameters, so biome names that contain spaces — for
example `root:Host-associated:Human:Digestive system` — need no special handling.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
This makes one request per protein, so keep `LIMIT` modest and be considerate of the
service, which is rate-limited. For thousands of sequences, query the release
remotely with [Parquet and DuckDB](../docs/mgnify-proteins-parquet-queries.qmd), or
take a [bulk download](../docs/ftp.md) instead.
:::

## Explore outwards from one protein

The biome ids in a detail response are the same ids the search endpoint accepts, so
you can start from a protein of interest and find others sharing its biome:

```{pyodide}
protein = get_json("protein/MGYP000261684433")

for biome in protein["biomes"]:
    print(biome["id"], biome["name"])
```

```{pyodide}
neighbours = search_proteins(
    biome_id=protein["biomes"][0]["id"],
    limit=10,
)

for hit in neighbours:
    print(hit["mgyp"])
```

## Running this code in your own environment

Install the package from a terminal:

```bash
python -m pip install requests
```

Run the Python cells in a notebook or script. To save the FASTA to a file instead of
downloading it from the browser, replace the download cell with:

```python
with open(fasta_filename, "w") as fasta_file:
    fasta_file.write(fasta_text)
```
